Featured Managers

Manager snapshot
Dave Fairchild
Dave Fairchild is the standard setter for the whole league: 6 titles, 17 playoff trips, and enough elite seasons to anchor the entire history view.
Manager snapshot
Brian Barna
Brian Barna was a repeat finisher, not a one-shot champion. 4 titles and 10 podiums make this one of the era-defining resumes.
Manager snapshot
Chris Perkins
Chris Perkins was a repeat finisher, not a one-shot champion. 2 titles and 7 podiums make this one of the era-defining resumes.
Manager snapshot
Craig Suchanec
Craig Suchanec was a repeat finisher, not a one-shot champion. 3 titles and 5 podiums make this one of the era-defining resumes.
Manager snapshot
Elissa Perkins
Elissa Perkins spent year after year in the mix. 8 playoff seasons and 4 podium finishes matter more here than one signature spike.
Manager snapshot
Jason Popovic
Jason Popovic had one of the swingier league arcs. The ceiling was real, but the path there was bumpier than the steady contenders.

Head-to-Head

Not every frequent matchup is a rivalry. This section tries to isolate the ones that actually mattered: close series, repeat playoff collisions, and pairings where one manager became the other’s recurring problem.

Defining rivalry
Brian Barna vs Dave Fairchild
41 games across 22 seasons, with 8 playoff meetings. Brian Barna has usually had the edge, but the real story is that this matchup kept mattering for a long time.
Closest long-run matchup
Joe Pariser vs Sean Riley
7 meetings across 5 seasons with an average margin of 15.675714285714282. This is the tightest rivalry that also held up over time.
Playoff foil
Brian Barna vs Dave Fairchild
8 playoff meetings across 41 total games. This is the rivalry to read if you care about blocked title paths more than regular-season volume.
How To Read Rivalries
  • Start with the defining rivalry to see which matchup held weight across the most seasons, not just the smallest average margin.
  • Use closest long-run matchup when you want the tightest rivalry that also lasted.
  • Use playoff foils when you care about who blocked title paths, not just who played often.
  • Use the heat map as a scan tool, then open the full matrix when you want the exact record and margin.

This section is here to protect trust. Older seasons still matter, but when the history is partial or suspect, the report should say so plainly instead of quietly letting shaky rows rewrite the story.

  • Headline records are filtered to remove clearly suspect rows such as zero-point team games and hidden-manager rows.
  • Historical anomalies are retained in validation tables so we can clean them over time instead of pretending the data is clean.
  • Cross-era comparisons require a multi-season sample before a manager appears in consistency and classification views.
  • Player-level record sections exclude partial player-data seasons such as 2003.
